curio.title: The tally sticks that burned down Parliament
curio.body: A tally stick was a wooden receipt: squared hazel, notched to record a sum, then split lengthwise so each party kept a half. Only the two original halves fit back together, so added notches would show. In 1834 the Exchequer ordered two cartloads of old tallies burned in the stoves under the House of Lords. By evening both chambers were lost, and J. M. W. Turner was in the crowd that watched.
